A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 20-page versions of the same MMFakeBench work. Text and rendered-page comparisons cover the methods, equations, tables, figures, and full appendix without material gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, MMD-Agent ablations, and supplementary analyses in Section 5 and Appendix 7.1, including Tables 2-6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the benchmark comparisons, ablations, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Figure 3 retain the same MMD-Agent procedure: hierarchical textual, visual, and cross-modal checks integrating rationales, actions, and external knowledge.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MMFakeBench coverage with 11,000 image-text pairs and 12 misinformation subcategories. Correcting NewsCLIPings to NewsCLIPpings in Section 3.1.3 does not change the source dataset.

E2.justification: Tables 2-3 and Appendix 7.2 retain the same LVLM configurations, six single-source detectors, and combined Mixed Detection baseline. Comparator participation is unchanged.

E3.justification: The 1,000-pair validation and 10,000-pair test splits, zero-shot evaluation, model configurations, metrics, response matching, and appendix binary-label mapping are unchanged.

E4.justification: The decomposition and rationale ablations in Table 3(b), misinformation-type analyses, instruction-following analysis, and error examples are identical, including Appendix 7.1 and 7.4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Statistical uncertainty reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings are retained, including Tables 2-6 and appendix examples. For example, Table 2 reports GPT-4V test macro-F1 of 48.8% with standard prompting and 61.5% with MMD-Agent in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical descriptions and Section 4 decision equation are identical. No definitions, assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark novelty, evaluation scope, limitations of existing detectors, and MMD-Agent effectiveness claims.

C2.justification: Performance interpretations and mechanism explanations are unchanged. Appendix 7.4-7.6 retains the same error interpretations, broader-impact discussion, and limitations of Wikipedia retrieval for challenging rumors.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-website link beneath the authors on page 1, providing a new access pointer. Implementation details and appendix prompts are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish any new code or data release.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, and research positioning are unchanged. The NewsCLIPpings spelling correction still refers to the same dataset and reference [21].

P1.justification: v2 corrects NewsCLIPings to NewsCLIPpings in Section 3.1.3 and updates the front matter with a project link and version/date stamp. There is no substantive rewriting or section reorganization.

P2.justification: The added link shifts Figure 1 and the abstract downward, moving another abstract line onto page 2. The spelling correction causes slight paragraph reflow; figure and table contents and all appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new project-page pointer and corrected dataset spelling offer small convenience and proofreading benefits. Methods, supporting evidence, substantive explanations, and the entire appendix remain unchanged, leaving overall paper quality essentially the same.
